current.text: He is reported to have a hip issue. Yahoo lists him as questionable with a quadriceps issue.
Experts agree his Yahoo price, a rank and ADP in the low to mid 20s, is too high. They see a rank in the 35 to 50 range as right and would not draft him in rounds 1 or 2. Pick 26 is called too early.
He is a category league bust at rank 23. He is reasonable in the 40s, and the expert does not expect huge minutes.
At ESPN's lower price, a rank around 51 or an ADP of 66, he is good value in category leagues.
In an auction mock he went for 27 USD. Josh would only pay about 21 to 22 USD.
His upside this season is more blocks and more three-point volume, around 18 points, 9 rebounds, 2 blocks and 1.7 threes.
He should keep a block rate of about 1.9 per game.
He had a poor playoff series against San Antonio. His coach says nobody is more trusted to improve over the summer.
He is not yet in his prime and should keep improving. The poor playoff series is expected to motivate him.
He is a projected starter next to Isaiah Hartenstein. The open rotation questions on OKC are in the frontcourt, with Hartenstein, Jaylin Williams and Thomas Sorber also in the mix.

OKC lost Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe. The team could be one of the lowest-volume three-point teams unless core players, Chet included, shoot more threes. The team is expected to push them to do so.
OKC is projected to win about 57 to 62 games and to be a top two seed in the West.
OKC has a league-minimum 13 back-to-backs. Its schedule is good with a March 28 end date.

durable.text: He is an All-NBA level real-life player, an elite defender and one of the two best rim protectors in the league, with great positioning.
Blocks are his outlier category, far above the top 250 pool.
His blocks make him look better in 9-cat z-score rankings than his real fantasy worth.
He gives few assists and few steals, and his three-point volume is modest. He can shoot a bit and is a decent scorer.
He had a broken hip season. His 55% on twos that season is probably an outlier. He shoots about 65% on twos when healthy.

note: The experts agree that Yahoo prices Chet too high, at a value of 29 USD and an average cost of 26.4 USD. Our league paid 32 USD for him last season. ESPN's 10 USD value and rank 52 are closer to the 35 to 50 range the experts like, so do not pay more than about 21 to 22 USD. He fits builds that want blocks, FG% and rebounds, but he gives little in assists and steals. Check early whether the hip or quad issue costs games, whether his minutes stay near 29 next to Hartenstein, and whether OKC really gets him to take more threes.
